content:
nina: FYI — Pilot kickoff with PegasusPay in 2H. They want a 48h technical POC to demonstrate API parity vs their existing vendor. Must-haves: identical webhook callbacks, preserved field names, and predictable token billing.

omar: I can put up a compatibility facade that rewrites our callbacks to their /events shape. Their consumers require X-Trace-Id and a top-level 'events' array. We should also preserve signature header X-Peg-Sig.

li: Product note — for generative summaries peg to model v2.1-compat and add a small prompt template to align style. Important: our tokenizer breaks some account numbers differently, so token counts will differ.

chris: Parity plan: 1) run 1.5k canonical prompts through both systems, 2) record token counts under both tokenizers, 3) compute semantic similarity and flag >12% variance. Will need a tiny Dedicated pool for deterministic runs (ETA 20h to prep).

morgan: Security asks: mTLS for callbacks, allowlisted egress IPs, and the completed security questionnaire. PegasusPay also requests a SOC2 excerpt and proof of KMS usage for persisted logs. I emailed ops for their SP/SAML metadata.

legal: They want a POC addendum: 30-day retention max, explicit non-use for model training, and liability scoped to the POC only. We can do that; confirm purge mechanism.

nina: Action items: @omar build callback facade + X-Peg-Sig mapping; @chris run parity suite; @morgan gather SOC2 and IPs; @legal draft addendum. Pegasus contact: integrations@pegasuspay.com.

chris: Quick curl we'll use for the smoke (replace API_KEY):

```
curl -X POST https://proxy.redwood.dev/pegasus/run \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"Summarize transaction ledger for Q1","callback_url":"https://hooks.pegasuspay.com/events"}'
```

Proxy will buffer streaming and POST final JSON to their callback with X-Trace-Id preserved and X-Peg-Sig computed.

li: For billing: tokenizers vary. We should present both counts side-by-side and offer a fixed trial credit (e.g., 100k tokens) for the POC. If they need exact parity billing we can run an invoiceable sample and compute a multiplier.

morgan: Netops requested our egress CIDRs: 44.55.66.0/24, 18.130.20.0/24 — sending to their firewall now. Uploaded SOC2_excerpt_redwood.pdf to the shared drive.

omar: Two technical caveats to call out in the demo: (1) slight micro-phrasing differences caused by decoding defaults, (2) streaming chunk boundaries — we buffer to ensure a single final callback to match their consumer. Deterministic mode (temp=0) reduces phrasing variance.

legal: Who owns purge? We will tag all POC data and schedule deletion at 30 days. @chris can you add the purge job and a short runbook?

chris: Ill add a purge job tied to the POC tag and push runbook to the drive. Also will include a CSV report of token multipliers.

ops-bot: provision: env=staging-pegasus-poc size=dedicated-micro region=us-east-1 status=ready

deploy-bot: deploy queued: branch=pegasus/compat-demo build=2031 ETA=5m :rocket:

nina: Current blockers: Pegasuss infra wants our egress IPs (done) and their security team asked for our SOC2 subreport (uploaded). If either of those stalls, escalate to AE. Goal: parity report + securityQA closed in 48h. :thumbsup:
